validity.recommendation: Check whether capacity 200 million cubic meters per day and diameter 1400 mm describe one pipe or the whole multi-line Uzhhorod to Veľké Kapušany crossing. Also check P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod), whose end section may be the same pipe, and P0780.
validity.researcher_notes: The crossing is real: Eustream lists Veľké Kapušany as the entry and exit point to Ukraine, and the Ukraine to Slovakia flow was halted on 1 January 2025. But Eustream describes four to five parallel pipes of mostly 48 and 56 inch at that point and a station entry flow of 220 million cubic meters per day. The sheet shows one pipe of 14.5 km, 1400 mm and 200 million cubic meters per day (7062.93 MMcf/d), which looks like a crossing total or a mixed value. No source found names this segment or its length. Possible overlap with the end of P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod), not settled on documents.

fills.researcher_notes: Both pages describe the crossing as natural gas infrastructure but do not name this line.
The start year is blank. The Uzhhorod to Veľké Kapušany crossing is Soviet-era trunk pipe. Searched Eustream pages and English language trade press. No source gives a start year for this segment.

The recorded 7062.93 MMcf/d equals 200 million cubic meters per day. Eustream says the Veľké Kapušany station allows an entry flow of 220 million cubic meters per day. That is the whole multi-line crossing, not one 14.5 km pipe. A system figure is not a source for this row. No segment figure found. See the concern on this row.

The recorded 14.5 km is not stated by any source found. Searched Eustream, Energy Community and trade press. Eustream describes four to five parallel pipelines at Veľké Kapušany, so the row may mix one pipe with the crossing.

The Eustream transmission page says the system is mostly 48 and 56 inch pipe, about 1220 and 1420 mm. That is a system description, not this segment, so it was not used. No source found names a 1400 mm diameter for this segment.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Eustream announced that from 1 January 2025 gas flow from Ukraine into Slovakia at Veľké Kapušany stopped, which ended Russian transit through this crossing in the forward direction. Eustream says other interconnection points keep working. No dated source found says whether the Ukrainian side of this crossing carries gas in the other direction. Searched Eustream, trade press and the Ukrainian press. Left unchanged until a source says it is idle or in use.
